newsitem.title: UK: Shield advances despite bid scepticism.
newsitem.headline: Shield advances despite bid scepticism.

text.p: Shares in British diagnostic company Shield Diagnostics Plc continued to advance strongly on Thursday despite market scepticism that the company could face a takeover bid.

Shares in Shield, which is developing a test which it believes will be able to predict propensity to heart attacks, were up 72 1/2 pence, or 14.5 percent, in late afternoon trading at 570 pence, close to an intra-day peak of 580 pence.
The shares have jumped by more than 35 percent since the start of the week after a weekend press report quoted people close the company speculating about possible bids.

After the report was picked up by the Times newspaper on Wednesday, British Biotech Plc denied that it had any interest in Shield, although reports said the two companies had considered a link in 1993.
Rumours were also circulating on Thursday that Drew Scientific Group Plc, which designs and makes diagnostic equipment, could be interested in Shield.
However an analyst close to Drew dismissed the speculation. Drew's market capitalisation is only around one-third of Shield's current valuation.

Analysts said other factors may have supported the stock. Shield is due to present further data from a British population study of the link between a blood clotting factor known as Activated Factor Twelve (AFT) and heart attacks at a conference in Florence.

And the company's brokers, UBS, told Reuters they intended to issue a research note on Shield shortly. Rumours were also circulating that Drew Scientific Group Plc, which also designs and makes diagnostic equipment, could be interested.
However, an analyst close to Drew dismissed the speculation. Drew's market capitalisation is only around one-third of Shield's current valuation.
Analysts said Shield was due to present further data from a British population study of the link between Activated Factor twelve and heart attacks at a conference in Florence next week.
Erling Refsum, analyst at Yamaichi International who has followed Shield closely for several years, said he thought British Biotech and Drew were unlikely bidders for Shield.
But he said Shield and its heart attack test could prove attractive to dominant diagnostic companies such as Abbott Laboratories Inc of the U.S.
"The fact that it is a bid target is valid," Refsum said, adding that the 10 stg bid price level suggested in press reports "is not unreasonable".

But another analyst, who asked not to be named, said this level was "slightly breathtaking". He said the gains in the Shield share price could provide an opportune moment for the Scottish company to strengthen its financial position through a rights issue.
